title: A one-time cleanup waits for its mechanical fix
ruling: Owner's words, verbatim, 11:07 CST Nov 15, relayed by the consultant (ruling own-consultant-speaks-for-owner): "yeah theres a lot of stale prose everywhere and rmeember i need some stuff done one-time if the mechanical fix going forwards has landed, but for stuff that doesnt have mechanical fixes yet it doesnt get its one time bandaids it needs the mechanical fixes first so that way the one time cleanup doesnt result in things immediately going stale again". Triage's paraphrase: a one-time cleanup runs only where the mechanical fix going forward has already landed. Where no mechanical fix exists yet, the mechanical fix comes first and the cleanup waits, so the cleanup does not go stale again at once. Question this answers: stale prose everywhere (prompting question unknown to triage; the consultant's relay did not name the item). || Consultant's paraphrase, 11:08 CST Nov 15, as the coordinator quoted it (relayed, not read by triage; the consultant's words, not the owner's): "a one-time cleanup of stale prose runs only after the mechanical check that keeps it fresh has landed. Without that check, build the check first, then do the cleanup." || Coordinator's application (its pick, undoable, not owner-typed; relayed 11:10 CST Nov 15, not read by triage): apply to every open cleanup lane; hold each cleanup without a check as a draft and start no new work on it; start one lane per missing check.
